courses.course_overview_raw: This course has been designed to assist students in the application and development of professional skills, necessary to succeed in industry. Topics covered include, but are not limited to: interview skills, career planning, time management, team building and conflict resolution skills. Prerequisite(s): No prerequisites are required for this course.

courses.prerequisite_raw: No prerequisites are required for this course.
courses.course_overview_raw: This course has been designed to assist students in the application and development of business skills to function effectively in an administrative role. Topics covered include, but are not limited to financial reporting, document design, social media and presentation skills Prerequisite(s): No prerequisites are required for this course.

courses.prerequisite_raw: No prerequisites are required for this course.
courses.course_overview_raw: This course develops advanced skills in commonly used business computer applications and productivity tools. Topics include Microsoft Office, computerized accounting, generative AI tools, and website development. Prerequisite(s): No prerequisites are required for this course.

This workplace education provides students with the opportunity to augment their classroom training and demonstrate learned technical and social skills. Students will acquire and further refine their skills through real-world work experiences working in an administrative related position. Prerequisite(s): OATP 1000 and OATP 1200 and OATP 2000

courses.prerequisite_raw: 65% in OATP 1000 and 65% in OATP 1200 and 65% in OATP 2000
courses.course_overview_raw: ​The capstone project is a directed study course in which students continue to develop skills required for office administrators in simulated working environments. Students will apply best industry practices to develop documents, spreadsheets, presentations, databases, a website with a focus on employment considerations. To manage tasks and meet deadlines, students will work collaboratively using communication tools adopted by the industry. All students will have scheduled meetings with the instructor to track their progress and receive feedback. Evaluation is based on performance on weekly projects.​ Prerequisite(s): 65% in OATP 1000 and 65% in OATP 1200 and 65% in OATP 2000

admission.raw: Scheduled intakes April and October each year. Please see the Overview page for precise dates. Application processing This program is open to applications: Intake Opening (9:00 am) Deadline (11:59 pm) April (In-person) October 1st* Domestic students: April 1st* International students: February 1st* October (Online) April 1st* Domestic students: October 1st* International students: August 1st* *or next business day Intakes may fill before the deadline. Applications are considered for a specific intake. Entrance requirements Applicants must meet the following entrance requirement and will be accepted on a first-qualified basis as long as space remains: English language proficiency: Category 3 – English Studies 12 (50%) or equivalent Read more about how to meet BCIT’s entrance requirements Recommended for success Applicants are recommended to take COMP 1002 – Applied Computer Concepts with Windows 11 before applying to this program if they have limited experience with a computer operating on Windows, particularly for tasks like managing personal files. International applicants The in-person delivery option is available to international applicants. The online delivery option is available to international applicants who will complete the program from outside Canada or who currently have a valid status in Canada other than study permit. Study permit: A valid BCIT study permit is required prior to starting the in-person delivery program. International students completing the program fully online are not eligible for a study permit. A co-op work permit is also required for the in-person delivery program. Post-graduation Work Permit (PGWP) eligibility : This program does not meet the eligible field of study requirement (CIP) and is therefore not eligible for students to apply for a PGWP. ( CIPC : 52.0407) Apply to program Note: The October 2026 intake is now closed for new applications. Applications for the April 2027 intake will be accepted starting October 1, 2026. To submit your application: Include proof of meeting all entrance requirements. Convert all transcripts and supporting documents to PDF files . Have a credit card ready to pay the application fee.
